name: Are older Los Angeles homes harder to remodel structurally?

mainEntity.name: Are older homes in Los Angeles, Pasadena, and Burbank harder to remodel structurally than newer homes?
mainEntity.text: Are older homes in Los Angeles, Pasadena, and Burbank harder to remodel structurally than newer homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older homes are often more challenging because the structure may not match modern expectations or original plans may be missing. Over time, many houses have been altered with additions, wall removals, patch repairs, or utility changes that complicate new remodeling work. Framing may be undersized by current standards, materials may have deteriorated, and hidden damage may only appear once surfaces are removed. That does not mean older homes cannot be remodeled well; it means they require more investigation and a more flexible budget. In practice, the design team may need to field-verify dimensions, inspect crawlspaces or attics, and plan for surprises. This is especially relevant in established neighborhoods where owners want open layouts but still need the home to behave safely and predictably. A thorough preconstruction assessment is the best way to control risk.
acceptedAnswer.description: Often yes. Older homes may have outdated framing, past additions, hidden damage, irregular dimensions, and fewer original drawings, which makes structural remodeling more uncertain and sometimes more expensive than remodeling a newer home.
